title: From Minimum Wage to Annual Salary: How Casual Loading and Super Affect Your Pay
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual pay using the 38-hour week. See how minimum wage, casual loading, and super guarantee affect your take-home and total package.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, working 38 hours per week, the annual gross pay is approximately $52,260 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How is annual salary calculated from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Annual gross pay is calculated by multiplying your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time position, we assume 38 hours per week. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour gives $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,260. This formula assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: Does casual loading apply to superannuation?
faqs.a: Yes, superannuation is paid on your ordinary time earnings, which for casual employees includes the 25% casual loading. So if your base rate is $26.44, your casual rate is $33.05, and super is calculated on that $33.05. The employer pays super on top of your gross pay, so your total employment cost is higher than your take-home plus super.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage (NMW) is the minimum hourly rate set by the Fair Work Commission, currently $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026. Award rates are industry or occupation-specific minimums set by the Fair Work Ombudsman, which are often higher than the NMW. Your actual minimum wage depends on your award or enterprise agreement. The NMW applies only if no award covers you.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Conversion

Converting your hourly rate to an annual salary is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. This gives you your gross annual pay before tax and super.

For example, if you earn the **National Minimum Wage** of $26.44 per hour, your annual gross pay is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,260. If you work a different number of hours each week, adjust accordingly. The formula also works for part-time or casual hours.

It can help to think in fortnights: your weekly pay multiplied by two. For the minimum wage, weekly pay is $1,004.90 (38 hours), so a fortnight is $2,009.80 before tax and super.

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage (NMW) is the legal minimum hourly rate set by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. This rate applies to employees not covered by an award or registered agreement.

Most employees, however, are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets a higher minimum wage for their industry or job. Award rates vary widely and often include penalty rates, allowances, and overtime provisions. The NMW is a floor, not a typical wage. For a more accurate figure for your role, check your award through the Fair Work Ombudsman or use our [pay guides](/blog) page.

## Casual Loading: What It Means for Your Rate

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of their base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (annual leave, sick leave, etc.). For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $26.44 + 25% = $33.05 per hour. This loading is included in your ordinary time earnings.

When using our [timesheet](/), you enter your base hourly rate, and a checkbox adds the 25% casual loading on top. Do not enter a rate that already includes the loading. The loading is calculated automatically.

Casual loading is not a bonus—it replaces entitlements. Your annual gross as a casual on the NMW working 38 hours per week would be $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,325. That is significantly higher than the permanent full-time equivalent, but you must budget for unpaid leave.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top of Your Gross

Superannuation is a compulsory contribution your employer makes into your super fund. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid on top of your gross pay. It does not come out of your pocket.

For a permanent full-time employee on the NMW, annual gross is $52,260, so super is $52,260 × 12% = $6,271.20. For a casual on the NMW, annual gross is $65,325, so super is $65,325 × 12% = $7,839. Super is capped at the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year.

Super is separate from your take-home pay. When comparing job offers, consider the total package: gross pay plus super. Our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains more.

## Tax and Medicare: What You Take Home

Your take-home pay is your gross pay minus income tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. For the 2025–26 year, single reduction thresholds apply (the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed in this estimate).

Using the NMW example: annual gross $52,260. Tax on $52,260: $0 on first $18,200, then 15% on $26,800 ($4,020), then 30% on $7,260 ($2,178) — total tax $6,198. Medicare levy 2% of $52,260 = $1,045.20. Take-home pay = $52,260 - $6,198 - $1,045.20 = $45,016.80. This is an estimate and does not include HELP repayments, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

For a more detailed breakdown, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

## Using the Timesheet and Other Tools

Our [timesheet](/), the home page, lets you enter your base hourly rate and toggle casual loading. It calculates your annual gross, fortnightly pay, super, and estimated tax. You can also explore our [reference tables](/data) for average earnings and tax brackets.

If you want to compare your rate to industry averages, the Australian Bureau of Statistics reports average weekly earnings. For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week, and all employees (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week. These are averages, not medians for your specific job. Our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page explains more.

## Key Takeaways

- Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. We assume 38 hours for full-time.
- The National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, but most workers are covered by higher award rates.
- Casual loading adds 25% to your base rate. Super is paid on your ordinary earnings, including casual loading.
- Tax and Medicare reduce your take-home pay. Use our tools to estimate.
- Always check your award or agreement for your correct minimum wage.

Remember, this is an estimate. Your actual pay may vary due to overtime, penalties, allowances, or salary sacrifice. For personalised advice, consult a qualified accountant or the Fair Work Ombudsman.
